title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: These may inform thee that I received thy kind letter, dated in the 4th month last–which was acceptable, although affecting to hear of thy getting such a hurt. We are in a good degree favored with health, for which with other blessings I wish to be thankful. We have had those worthy’s to visit us. As thee mentioned in thy letter, Joseph Potts was at the Quarterly Meeting, & a heart tendering season it was to many. Elias Hicks in a short time after which will not be easily forgot, yet, after all those gospel showers there doth not appear that improvement amongst us as is desirable. I fear we shall be like the ground that dranketh the rain & brought forth briars & thorns, yet believe there is like to be a growth in some places. There has been very rapid progress of Friends settling over the Ohio from different parts, but the largest number are from North Carolina. There appears large fields of labor open & opening; may the number of rightly qualified laborers be abundantly increased. That those that have been heretofore engaged may be encouraged and reanimated to persevere on conquering everything that opposes truth. It would be very acceptable to us to see thee in our parts, if thy way should open rightly for it.

Our brother Robert is now living at Bridgeport. They are in a middling state of health. At present he is shoemaking, & plenty of work. I do not know that I can say much more that would be agreeable, for discontent continues to frequent their dwelling and poverty is a near neighbor. Grandeur too intimate in the family, and tender sympathy with true uniting love & harmony too much of a stranger, that I wish they had that cordial which makes hard things easy & bittersweet &. I wish desire what I have wrote may be rightly understood, except its likely he will write & perhaps give thee a more satisfactory account. Therefore don’t expose my poor scribble if thou canst make out to read thyself, it may be sufficient.

closer.salute: Therefore, with love to you all wife & children, with others as if named I conclude, thy affectionate sister,
